title: Choice-chamber experiment: do mealworms avoid light?

stimulus.title: A choice chamber for mealworm larvae
stimulus.html: Mealworms are the larvae of a beetle that lives in stored grain. A student notices that mealworms in a tray of bran gather under a piece of cardboard. To test whether they move away from light, the student builds a choice chamber: a clear plastic box divided into two equal halves with an open doorway between them, and a lamp above it. One half is covered with black paper. Ten mealworms are placed on the line between the halves, and the number in each half is recorded after 10 minutes.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Identify the independent variable and the dependent variable in this investigation.

rubric.point: Independent variable: light (light or dark half / light intensity). Dependent variable: the number (or percentage) of mealworms in each half after 10 minutes. Both are needed for the point.
accept: IV: presence of light; DV: number of mealworms in each half
IV: light vs dark; DV: where the mealworms end up after 10 minutes
IV: light intensity; DV: percentage of larvae in the dark side

parts.sample: Independent variable: light, whether a half is lit or covered (dark). Dependent variable: the number of mealworms in each half after 10 minutes.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: State the null hypothesis for this investigation.

rubric.point: Light has no effect on where mealworms go: equal numbers (5 and 5) are expected in the two halves, and any difference is due to chance.
accept: mealworms show no preference between the light and dark halves
the distribution of mealworms is the same in both halves
any difference between the numbers in the two halves is due to chance

parts.sample: Null hypothesis: light has no effect on where the mealworms go, so equal numbers are expected in the light and dark halves, and any difference is due to chance.

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: The black paper may also make the covered half warmer or cooler than the lit half. Describe how the student could change the design so that any preference can be attributed to light, and justify the change.

rubric.point: Describes a way to remove or control the temperature difference, with a reason: place a water bath or heat filter between lamp and box (or use an LED/cool light), measure and match the temperature of both halves with thermometers, or run a control chamber with both halves covered/both lit to check for side preference; justified by keeping all variables other than light the same.
accept: put a heat-absorbing water filter under the lamp and check both halves are the same temperature, so only light differs
use a cool LED light and thermometers in both halves to show temperature is equal
run a control chamber with both halves dark to show the animals have no preference without a light difference

parts.sample: The student should put a clear tray of water between the lamp and the box to absorb heat, place a thermometer in each half, and start counting only when both halves are at the same temperature. Then light is the only condition that differs between the halves, so a preference can be attributed to light rather than to temperature.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: Suppose 46 of 50 mealworms in five chambers end up in the dark half. The student wants to know whether the mealworms steer away from light (a taxis) or just move faster in light and slow down in the dark (a kinesis). Propose an additional observation or experiment that could distinguish these two explanations.

rubric.point: Proposes tracking individual mealworms (filming or marking their paths) and comparing speed and direction: a taxis shows movement directed away from the light source (for example, turning away when the light is moved), while a kinesis shows faster movement in light and slower movement in the dark with no consistent direction. Accept moving the lamp to the side and checking whether paths are aimed away from it.
accept: film individual mealworms and measure their speed and direction in each half
move the light to one end of a uniformly lit tray and see whether mealworms turn away from it
release mealworms in an evenly lit tray and in an evenly dark tray and compare their speeds

parts.sample: Film single mealworms in an evenly lit tray, an evenly dark tray, and a tray lit from one side only. If they move faster in light and slow down in the dark but go in no particular direction, that is a kinesis. If, in the tray lit from one side, they turn and crawl directly away from the lamp, that is a taxis (negative phototaxis).
